readings.title: Penalties for Disobedience
readings.subtitle: Laws Concerning Molek, Mediums, and Immorality
readings.text: [Leviticus 20:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [2] <dq>“And say to the children of Yisra’ĕl, ‘Any man of the children of Yisra’ĕl, or of the strangers who sojourn in Yisra’ĕl, who gives any of his offspring to Molek, shall certainly be put to death. The people of the land shall stone him with stones.</dq> [3] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> shall set <dn>My</dn> face against that man, and cut him off from the midst of his people, because he has given of his offspring to Molek, to defile <dn>My</dn> set-apart place and to profane <dn>My</dn> set-apart Name.</dq> [4] <dq>‘And if the people of the land at all hide their eyes from the man when he gives any of his offspring to Molek, and they do not kill him,</dq> [5] <dq>then <dn>I</dn> shall set <dn>My</dn> face against that man and against his clan, and cut him off from the midst of their people, and all who go whoring after him, to whore after Molek.</dq> [6] <dq>‘And the being who turns to mediums and to spiritists, to go whoring after them, <dn>I</dn> shall set <dn>My</dn> face against that being and cut him off from the midst of his people.</dq> [7] <dq>‘Set yourselves apart, therefore, and be set-apart, for <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq> [8] <dq>‘And you shall guard <dn>My</dn> laws and do them. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> who sets you apart.</dq> [9] <dq>‘For everyone who curses his father or his mother shall certainly be put to death. He has cursed his father or his mother, his blood is upon him.</dq> [10] <dq>‘And a man who commits adultery with the wife of another man, who commits adultery with the wife of his neighbour: the adulterer and the adulteress shall certainly be put to death.</dq> [11] <dq>‘And a man who lies with his father’s wife has uncovered his father’s nakedness. Both of them shall certainly be put to death, their blood is upon them.</dq> [12] <dq>‘And a man who lies with his daughter-in-law: both of them shall certainly be put to death. They have done perversion, their blood is upon them.</dq> [13] <dq>‘And a man who lies with a male as he lies with a woman: both of them have done an abomination. They shall certainly be put to death, their blood is upon them.</dq> [14] <dq>‘And a man who takes a woman and her mother: it is wicked. They burn him and them with fire, that there be no wickedness in your midst.</dq> [15] <dq>‘And a man who gives his emission to a beast shall certainly be put to death, and you shall kill the beast.</dq> [16] <dq>‘And a woman who approaches any beast and mates with it: you shall kill the woman and the beast. They shall certainly be put to death, their blood is upon them.</dq> [17] <dq>‘And a man who takes his sister, his father’s daughter or his mother’s daughter, and sees her nakedness and she sees his nakedness: it is a shame. And they shall be cut off before the eyes of the children of their people. He has uncovered his sister’s nakedness, he bears his crookedness.</dq> [18] <dq>‘And a man who lies with a woman during her sickness and uncovers her nakedness: he has exposed her flow, and she has uncovered the flow of her blood. Both of them shall be cut off from their people.</dq> [19] <dq>‘And do not uncover the nakedness of your mother’s sister or of your father’s sister, for he has uncovered his near of kin. They bear their crookedness.</dq> [20] <dq>‘And a man who lies with his aunt has uncovered his uncle’s nakedness. They bear their sin, they die childless.</dq> [21] <dq>‘And a man who takes his brother’s wife: it is an unclean thing. He has uncovered his brother’s nakedness, they are childless.</dq> [22] <dq>‘And you shall guard all <dn>My</dn> laws and all <dn>My</dn> right-rulings, and do them, so that the land where <dn>I</dn> am bringing you to dwell does not vomit you out.</dq> [23] <dq>‘And do not walk in the laws of the nation which <dn>I</dn> am driving out before you, for they committed all these, and <dn>I</dn> loathed them.</dq> [24] <dq>‘But <dn>I</dn> have said to you, “You are to possess their land, and <dn>I</dn> <dn>Myself</dn> give it to you to possess it, a land flowing with milk and honey.” <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, who has separated you from the peoples.</dq> [25] <dq>‘And you shall make a distinction between clean beasts and unclean, and between unclean birds and clean. And do not make your beings abominable by beast, or by bird, or by whatever creeps on the ground, which <dn>I</dn> have separated from you as unclean.</dq> [26] <dq>‘And you shall be set-apart to <dn>Me</dn>, for <dn>I</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> am set-apart, and have separated you from the peoples to be <dn>Mine</dn>.</dq> [27] <dq>‘And a man or a woman in whom is a medium or a spiritist shall certainly be put to death. They stone them with stones, their blood is upon them.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: Holiness of the Priesthood
readings.subtitle: Instructions for Aharon and His Sons
readings.text: [Leviticus 21:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“Speak to the priests, the sons of Aharon, and say to them, ‘No one is to be defiled for the dead among his people,</dq> [2] <dq>except for his relatives who are nearest to him: his mother, his father, his son, his daughter, and his brother;</dq> [3] <dq>also his maiden sister who is near to him, who has had no husband, for her he is defiled.</dq> [4] <dq>‘A husband does not defile himself among his people, to profane himself.</dq> [5] <dq>‘They do not make any baldness on their heads, nor do they shave the corner of their beard, nor do they make any cuttings in their flesh.</dq> [6] <dq>‘They are set-apart to their <dn>Elohim</dn>, and they do not profane the Name of their <dn>Elohim</dn>, for they bring the offerings of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> made by fire, and the bread of their <dn>Elohim</dn>, therefore they shall be set-apart.</dq> [7] <dq>‘They do not take a woman who is a whore or a defiled woman, nor do they take a woman put away from her husband. For he is set-apart to his <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq> [8] <dq>‘And you shall set him apart, for he brings the bread of your <dn>Elohim</dn>. He is set-apart to you, for <dn>I</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, setting you apart, am set-apart.</dq> [9] <dq>‘And the daughter of any priest, if she profanes herself by whoring, she profanes her father. She is burned with fire.</dq> [10] <dq>‘And the high priest among his brothers, on whose head the anointing oil was poured and who is ordained to wear the garments, does not unbind his head nor tear his garments,</dq> [11] <dq>nor come near any dead body, nor defile himself for his father or his mother.</dq> [12] <dq>‘Nor does he go out of the set-apart place, nor profane the set-apart place of his <dn>Elohim</dn>, for the sign of dedication of the anointing oil of his <dn>Elohim</dn> is upon him. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [13] <dq>‘And he takes a wife in her maidenhood.</dq> [14] <dq>‘A widow or a divorced woman or a defiled woman or a whore, these he does not take, but a maiden of his own people he takes as wife.</dq> [15] <dq>‘And he does not profane his offspring among his people, for <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> who sets him apart.’ ”</dq> [16] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [17] <dq>“Speak to Aharon, saying, ‘No man of your offspring throughout their generations who has any defect approaches to bring the bread of his <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq> [18] <dq>‘For any man who has a defect does not approach: a man blind or lame, who is disfigured or deformed,</dq> [19] <dq>or a man who has a broken foot or a broken hand,</dq> [20] <dq>or is a hunchback, or a dwarf, or a man who has a defect in his eye, or eczema or scab, or is a eunuch.</dq> [21] <dq>‘No man of the offspring of Aharon the priest who has a defect comes near to bring the offerings made by fire to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. He has a defect, he does not come near to bring the bread of his <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq> [22] <dq>‘He eats the bread of his <dn>Elohim</dn>, both the most set-apart and the set-apart,</dq> [23] <dq>only he does not go near the veil or approach the slaughter-place, because he has a defect, lest he profane <dn>My</dn> set-apart places. For <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> who sets them apart.’ ”</dq> [24] And Mosheh spoke to Aharon and to his sons, and to all the children of Yisra’ĕl. [Leviticus 22:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [2] <dq>“Speak to Aharon and to his sons, that they separate themselves from the set-apart gifts of the children of Yisra’ĕl, which they set apart to <dn>Me</dn>, that they do not profane <dn>My</dn> set-apart Name. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [3] <dq>“Say to them, ‘Any man of all your offspring throughout your generations who draws near to the set-apart gifts which the children of Yisra’ĕl set apart to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, while he is unclean, that being shall be cut off from <dn>My</dn> presence. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [4] <dq>‘Any man of the offspring of Aharon, who is a leper or has a flow, does not eat the set-apart gifts until he is clean. And whoever touches what is made unclean by a body, or a man who has an emission of semen,</dq> [5] <dq>or a man who touches any creeping creature by which he would be made unclean, or any person by whom he would be made unclean, whatever his uncleanness.</dq> [6] <dq>‘The being who touches it shall be unclean until evening, and does not eat the set-apart gifts unless he has bathed his body in water.</dq> [7] <dq>‘And when the sun goes down he shall be clean, and afterwards eat the set-apart gifts, because it is his food.</dq> [8] <dq>‘That which dies or is torn he does not eat, to defile himself with it. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [9] <dq>‘And they shall guard <dn>My</dn> charge, lest they bear sin for it and die thereby, if they profane it. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> who sets them apart.</dq> [10] <dq>‘And no stranger eats the set-apart gift, a sojourner with the priest or a hired servant does not eat the set-apart gift.</dq> [11] <dq>‘But when the priest buys a person with his silver, he eats of it. And one born in his house, they eat of his food.</dq> [12] <dq>‘And if a priest’s daughter is married to a stranger, she does not eat of the set-apart offerings.</dq> [13] <dq>‘But if a priest’s daughter is a widow or divorced, and has no child, and has returned to her father’s house as in her youth, she eats her father’s food. But no stranger eats of it.</dq> [14] <dq>‘And when a man eats the set-apart gift by mistake, then he shall add one-fifth to it, and give it to the priest with the set-apart gift.</dq> [15] <dq>‘And they do not profane the set-apart gifts of the children of Yisra’ĕl, which they lift up to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>,</dq> [16] <dq>or allow them to bear the crookedness of trespass when they eat their set-apart gifts. For <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> who sets them apart.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: Acceptable Offerings
readings.subtitle: Without Blemish
readings.text: [Leviticus 22:17] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [18] <dq>“Speak to Aharon and to his sons, and to all the children of Yisra’ĕl, and say to them, ‘Any man of the house of Yisra’ĕl or of the strangers in Yisra’ĕl who brings his offering for any of his vows or for any of his voluntary offerings, which they bring to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> for a burnt offering:</dq> [19] <dq>for your acceptance, it is a male, a perfect one, from the cattle, from the sheep, or from the goats.</dq> [20] <dq>‘Whatever has a defect, you do not bring, for it is not acceptable for you.</dq> [21] <dq>‘And when a man brings a peace offering to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, to separate a vow or a voluntary offering from the cattle or the sheep, it is to be perfect to be accepted, let there be no defect in it.</dq> [22] <dq>‘Those blind or broken or maimed, or having an ulcer or eczema or scabs, you do not bring to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, nor make an offering by fire of them on the slaughter-place to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [23] <dq>‘As for a bull or a lamb that has any limb deformed or dwarfed, you make it a voluntary offering, but for a vow it is not accepted.</dq> [24] <dq>‘And that which has its testicles bruised or crushed or torn or cut, you do not bring to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, nor do you do this in your land.</dq> [25] <dq>‘And from a stranger’s hand you do not bring the food of your <dn>Elohim</dn> from any of these, because their corruption is in them, defects are in them, they are not accepted for you.’ ”</dq> [26] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [27] <dq>“When a bull or a sheep or a goat is born, it shall be seven days under its mother. And from the eighth day and thereafter it is accepted as an offering made by fire to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [28] <dq>“But a cow or a sheep, do not kill it and its young on the same day.</dq> [29] <dq>“And when you make an offering of thanksgiving to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, make it for your acceptance.</dq> [30] <dq>“It is eaten that same day, leave none of it until morning. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [31] <dq>“And you shall guard <dn>My</dn> commands and do them. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [32] <dq>“And do not profane <dn>My</dn> set-apart Name, and <dn>I</dn> shall be set-apart among the children of Yisra’ĕl. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> who sets you apart,</dq> [33] <dq>who brought you out of the land of Mitsrayim, to be your <dn>Elohim</dn>. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.”</dq>
